Miedzyrzec Podlaski New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Międzyrzec Podlaski, Poland

Not demolished. This is the newer of Międzyrzec Podlaski's two Jewish cemeteries, established in 1810 and gradually expanded to more than five times its original size over the 19th century. During WWII, German soldiers took the cemetery's most valuable stone tombstones back to Germany itself, while sandstone and rock matzevot were used locally for construction; Holocaust victims were buried here in mass graves. In 1946, Abram and Sara Finkelsztejn of New York funded repairs to the cemetery wall, into which several hundred recovered tombstones from the town and surrounding area were built, alongside new concrete markers commemorating individuals and groups; a second monument was funded by New York Jews in 1995. The cemetery remained open until at least 1973, when its final burial took place. Eleven surviving cast-iron tombstones, dated 1833 to 1943 and made from local ironwork, are a distinctive feature of the site.
